points.quote: Generative AI may be used as a tool to support student work unless otherwise specified in an assignment brief, but it is essential that every student’s work remains original.
points.gist: Generative AI may be used to support student work unless an assignment brief says otherwise, but work must remain original.

points.quote: All use of generative AI must be acknowledged in an ‘Acknowledgements’ section on the first page of any piece of academic work where it has been used. This includes the use of translation tools.
points.gist: All generative AI use, including translation tools, must be acknowledged in an Acknowledgements section on the first page of the work.

points.quote: Name and version of the generative AI system used, e.g., ChatGPT-3.5
points.gist: The acknowledgement must give the name and version of the generative AI system used, for example ChatGPT-3.5.

points.quote: Brief description (single sentence) of how the tool was used
points.gist: The acknowledgement must include a single-sentence description of how the tool was used.

points.quote: AI-generated answers presented as a student’s own work
points.gist: AI-generated answers presented as a student's own work is listed as a type of academic misconduct.

points.quote: Extensive and deliberate use of artificial intelligence where it was not permitted or with the intention to untruthfully and unreasonably claim the work is original.
points.gist: Extensive and deliberate AI use where not permitted, or to falsely claim originality, counts as gross academic misconduct.

points.quote: Misconduct arises from the inclusion of unattributed material, including AI sources, as opposed to solely the misuse of citation conventions.
points.gist: Including unattributed material, including AI sources, rather than only misusing citation conventions is a criterion for major academic misconduct.

points.quote: Failure of module with no reassessment and recommendation to the Course Assessment Board that the failed module should impact on any progression or award entitlement, with no opportunity to restudy that or an alternative module.
points.anchor: Table 3: Penalties for Academic Misconduct (Taught Students)
points.gist: A penalty is module failure with no reassessment, a recommendation that it affect progression or award, and no opportunity to restudy.

points.quote: Using AI to conduct statistical analysis for you represents academic misconduct.
points.anchor: Appendix 1: Illustrative examples of acceptable use of AI tools
points.gist: Using AI to conduct statistical analysis for you represents academic misconduct.

points.quote: Some work has been flagged as major misconduct as the statistical tests conducted by AI were highly unusual, overly advanced, or contained inaccuracies and unusual reporting of results. This led to failure of the module.
points.anchor: Appendix 1: Illustrative examples of acceptable use of AI tools
points.gist: Some work was flagged as major misconduct because AI-run statistical tests were unusual, overly advanced or inaccurate, leading to module failure.

points.quote: Such tools can only ever be used if participants have given signed agreement to this, use of such tools was agreed by the ethics committee, and all participant data must be anonymised.
points.anchor: Appendix 1: Illustrative examples of acceptable use of AI tools
points.gist: Interview transcription tools can only be used with participants' signed agreement, ethics committee agreement, and anonymised participant data.

points.quote: Notes, handouts and slides created by lecturers represent their intellectual property and should never be uploaded into AI without their explicit permission to do so.
points.anchor: Appendix 1: Illustrative examples of acceptable use of AI tools
points.gist: Lecturers' notes, handouts and slides are their intellectual property and should never be uploaded into AI without explicit permission.

points.quote: Some transcription tools offer coding and thematic analysis functions. This represents academic misconduct as it involves AI thinking for you.
points.anchor: Appendix 1: Illustrative examples of acceptable use of AI tools
points.gist: Using transcription tools' coding and thematic analysis functions represents academic misconduct because it involves AI thinking for you.

points.quote: Use of the AI-functionality in tools such as Grammarly and Co-Pilot as well as other AI tools such as Chat-GPT, Scite AI etc. to draft content.
points.anchor: Appendix 1: Illustrative examples of acceptable use of AI tools
points.gist: Using AI functionality in tools such as Grammarly, Co-Pilot, ChatGPT or Scite AI to draft content is listed as unacceptable.

points.quote: The student will need to provide clear evidence of their authorship of the work, for example, dated files or screenshots providing evidence of research and planning or evidence of prompts used and outputs generated.
points.gist: A student disputing an AI misconduct judgment must give clear evidence of authorship, such as dated files, screenshots, or prompts and outputs.

points.quote: students are encouraged to keep a record of any AI usage (e.g. saved searches).
points.gist: Students are encouraged to keep a record of any AI usage, such as saved searches.

points.quote: Handing in work that sounds like it has been written by AI means your work may be investigated for misconduct.
points.anchor: Appendix 1: Illustrative examples of acceptable use of AI tools
points.gist: Handing in work that sounds like it was written by AI means it may be investigated for misconduct.
